title: Perplexity Decider Integration: Setup Guide (2026)
summary: Perplexity Decider integration connects the Sonar API to your workflow without code, letting you test on real tickets before self-hosting.
body_markdown:
## Running the Decision Step in Activepieces


### Set up and test response branching


You can call Perplexity from a trigger and branch on the answer in Activepieces without writing code, and the free plan's 1,000 credits a month cover a test on your twenty tickets; when they run out, flows stay on and runs wait until the credits refresh.


An unresolved error can land in a human queue instead of closing a ticket.


Zapier or Make can build the same flow; pick whichever your team already pays for. I haven't verified anything about the Perplexity connector beyond what the screenshot below shows.


What I can point to is the catalogue it would sit in: Activepieces counts 750 integrations in the packages/integrations/community directory of its MIT-licensed open source repo, and its Integrations Framework and MCP Server documentation describe the same integration action that runs as a step in your flow being exposed as a tool on the per-project MCP server, reachable from Claude, ChatGPT or Cursor.


So a decision step you build and test here can later be called by an agent without being rebuilt, and MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run Activepieces in production.


Create the key in your Perplexity account's API settings, then paste it into a new Perplexity connection in Activepieces. Give the connection a name that says what it's for. If a key leaks, you want to know which flow to pause.


Run the step once with a fixed, harmless question before wiring anything else. One successful response tells you the key, the connection and the step all work. If it fails here, nothing downstream is the cause.


### Prompt Perplexity for one word and branch


Tell the model to reply with one word from a list you give it, such as "refund", "bug" or "unclear". A free-text paragraph can't be branched on. Always include "unclear", so a confusing email has somewhere safe to go.


In the flow below, a Fillout form response starts things off and passes through Perplexity AI and a text step.


It then splits at a Router into a branch that runs a second Perplexity step and creates a HubSpot company, plus an Otherwise path with nothing on it yet.


Your Otherwise path is where "unclear" and failures belong.


Build the same way: route on the exact category words, and put the human-review step on Otherwise. Check the retry options on each step in the builder on the date you build.


A retry that quietly repeats a bad call is worse than a visible failure.


### Test the workflow and check the cost


Use one clear case, one angry email and one message that fits no category. The angry email is the real test: confirm it reaches a person, not an automatic reply. Then look at what a run costs you.


On its[pricing page](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) ,[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) lists three plans. Free is $0 per month, so you can build and test this flow before spending anything.


Plus is $20 per month, a small sum if one run saves a mishandled complaint. Team is $200 per month, ten times Plus, so move up only when several people need to work in the same flows.


Check the page again on your build date, because plan limits change.
